description: Regalis is a small student team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge with a shared passion for space exploration and storytelling. With programming, writing and visual design, we created a project suitable for younger audiences
summary: We developed a simple visual novel surrounding the abandoned spacecrafts on both The Moon and Mars. Both celestial bodies will have a story of its own, following a main character. The chosen main character will explore and meet other spacecrafts that has been sent many years ago, eventually getting to know more about them.
details: Our project is a click-based, dialogue-driven visual novel featuring two playable routes: Mars and the Moon. Players advance through conversations with iconic NASA spacecraft, reading about their real mission histories, discoveries, and final days through character-driven storytelling. Visual novels are especially popular among children and teenagers, making this format an effective way to capture younger audiences who might normally find raw mission data or textbooks intimidating. By relying on stylized 2D sprites, our approach also keeps development fast, lightweight, and easy to run on everyday student laptops without specialized hardware. Our goal is to spark curiosity about space exploration among younger audiences by introducing them not only to active missions, but also to historic and inactive spacecraft that are often overlooked. We built the game using Ren'Py, an open-source visual novel engine powered by Python and Ren'Py's scripting language. Besides that, we also selected clear typography and bite-sized dialogue pacing tailored for younger readers.
